title: Ampleness descends to a stage of an affine transition limit
statement: Let $I$ be a small nonempty directed set, $(Z_i)_{i\in I}$ an inverse system of quasi-compact schemes [def-weil-pbc-quasi-compact-scheme] that are quasi-separated [def-weil-quasi-separated-morphism], with affine transition morphisms $q_{ji}:Z_j\to Z_i$ for $j\geq i$ [pqf-def-affine-morphism]. Let $Z=\varprojlim_i Z_i$ with projections $q_i$ be the limit in schemes [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-pbc-category-colimit], and fix $i_0\in I$. Let $L_0$ be an invertible $\mathcal O_{Z_{i_0}}$-module [def-sc-invertible-module]. If $q_{i_0}^*L_0$ is ample [def-weil-pbc-ample-invertible-module] on $Z$, then there exists $j\geq i_0$ such that $q_{j i_0}^*L_0$ is ample on $Z_j$. The pullbacks are tensor pullbacks [def-pc-module-pullback].

proof.text: Because $q_{i_0}^*L_0$ is ample, the ampleness definition gives, for every point of $Z$, a section of some positive tensor power whose nonvanishing open is affine. Quasi-compactness of $Z$ lets us choose finitely many such sections $s_1,\ldots,s_m$ (possibly of different powers) whose affine nonvanishing opens $Z_{s_a}$ cover $Z$.

source.place: Tag 09MT proof, first sentence; Properties, Definition 01PS

proof.text: Because $L_0$ is invertible, it is quasi-coherent by [def-sc-invertible-module]. Apply [lem-sc-valuation-limit-qcoh-section-descent] to the tail above $i_0$ with $F_{i_0}=L_0$: for each chosen section $s_a$ there are an index $i_a\ge i_0$ and a section $s_{a,i_a}$ of the pullback of $L_0$ to $Z_{i_a}$ whose pullback to $Z$ is $s_a$. A common upper bound $i_2$ of the finitely many $i_a$ gives sections $s_{a,i_2}$ on one stage, all pulling back to $s_a$.

Fix $a$. The principal open $(Z_{i_2})_{s_{a,i_2}}$ has inverse image $Z_{s_a}$ in $Z$, because pullback of a section of an invertible module pulls back its nonvanishing locus. By [lem-weil-pbc-limit-affine-transition], the inverse images of this open form an inverse system with affine transitions and limit $Z_{s_a}$. The latter is affine by Step 1, so [lem-weil-pbc-limit-affine-stage] gives an index $j_a\ge i_2$ such that $(Z_j)_{s_{a,j}}$ is affine for every $j\ge j_a$.

source.place: Tag 09MT proof, invoking Lemma 01Z6 (lemma-limit-affine) after descending the sections

proof.text: Choose a common upper bound $j_0$ of the finitely many $j_a$. Pulling the sections forward to $Z_{j_0}$ preserves affineness of their principal opens because each transition morphism is affine. Their inverse images in $Z$ still cover $Z$, so the union $W_{j_0}=\bigcup_a(Z_{j_0})_{s_{a,j_0}}$ has inverse image equal to $Z$. Apply clause (2) of [pqf-lem-limit-qc-open-descends] to the quasi-compact opens $W_{j_0}$ and $Z_{j_0}$, whose inverse images in the limit agree; after increasing to some $j\ge j_0$ their pullbacks are equal. Thus the finitely many affine principal opens $(Z_j)_{s_{a,j}}$ cover $Z_j$.

source.place: Tag 09MT proof, final use of Lemma 01YX/lemma-descend-opens

proof.text: The module on $Z_j$ is invertible, the sections $s_{a,j}$ have affine nonvanishing opens, and those opens cover the quasi-compact scheme $Z_j$. By the definition of an ample invertible module [def-weil-pbc-ample-invertible-module], its pullback $q_{j i_0}^*L_0$ is ample on $Z_j$.
